title: Combinatorial Identities of Three Complex Parameters and Their Basic Applications
content: Inspired by a problem proposal recently published in the journal The Fibonacci Quarterly we offer a generalization consisting of two combinatorial identities involving three complex parameters.  These identities turn out to be immensely rich. We demonstrate this by providing basic applications to four different fields:  polynomial identities, trigonometric identities, identities involving Horadam numbers, and combinatorial identities. Many of our findings will generalize existing results.
